steps.tx: A hard crystalline stone forming inside the kidney is a **renal calculus**. Most stones contain calcium oxalate, while infection stones contain phosphate mixtures. Stones cause pain only when they move or block urine flow. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: A renal calculus is a hard kidney stone that hurts only when it moves or blocks urine flow.

vis.alt: Plain KUB film showing a renal calculus.
vis.caption: Renal calculus visible on a plain kidney film. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: A large branched stone filling the renal pelvis and calyces is a **staghorn calculus**. It grows in infected alkaline urine and slowly destroys kidney tissue if ignored. Complete stone clearance is needed because fragments regrow quickly. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: A staghorn calculus branches through the kidney in infected urine and destroys tissue unless fully cleared.

vis.alt: Staghorn calculus filling the renal pelvis and calyces.
vis.caption: Staghorn calculus: branched stone filling the collecting system. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Severe loin pain radiating to the groin from a moving ureteric stone is **ureteric colic**. The patient rolls around unable to find comfort, unlike the still patient with peritonitis. Blood in the urine commonly accompanies the pain. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Ureteric colic sends severe loin pain to the groin and makes the patient roll around restlessly.

vis.alt: Renal colic pain radiation from loin to groin.
vis.caption: Renal colic: loin to groin pain from a ureteric stone. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The best first scan for a suspected urinary stone is a **NCCT KUB**. This non contrast computed tomography of kidneys, ureters and bladder shows stone size and position accurately. It also reveals kidney swelling from obstruction. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: A non contrast CT of the urinary tract best shows stone size, position and kidney swelling.

steps.tx: The ureter narrows naturally at three places known as the **sites of ureteric narrowing**. Stones lodge at the pelviureteric junction, where the ureter crosses the pelvic brim, and where it enters the bladder. Knowing these sites helps predict where a stone will stick.
steps.say: Stones lodge at three natural narrowings: the junction, the pelvic brim crossing, and the bladder entry.

steps.tx: Shock waves focused from outside the body to break a stone are called **ESWL**. Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy suits many kidney and upper ureter stones without any cut. Fragments then pass naturally in the urine over days. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Shock wave treatment breaks stones from outside the body so fragments can pass naturally in urine.

vis.alt: Interventional options for urinary stones including shock waves and keyhole surgery.
vis.caption: Stone treatment options: shock waves, endoscopy and keyhole surgery. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Keyhole surgery through the back directly into the kidney is **PCNL**. Percutaneous nephrolithotomy removes large and staghorn stones through a small tract. It clears big stone burdens better than shock wave treatment alone. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: Keyhole surgery through the back removes large and staghorn stones through a small tract into the kidney.

steps.tx: Passing a fine scope up the ureter to see and laser a stone is **ureteroscopy**. It treats most ureteric stones and many kidney stones in one sitting. A temporary stent often follows to keep the ureter open while swelling settles. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Ureteroscopy passes a fine scope up the ureter to laser stones, often leaving a temporary stent afterwards.

steps.tx: An infected kidney blocked by a stone is a surgical emergency needing urgent **decompression**. Antibiotics alone cannot reach pus behind an obstruction. A stent or a drainage tube through the back relieves pressure until the stone is treated later. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: An infected blocked kidney needs urgent drainage by stent or back tube because antibiotics cannot reach trapped pus.
